hero.lead: An island nation of 933,000 across the Pacific, where 97 in every hundred complete lower-secondary school and the nation’s first sovereign blue bond funds coastal protection.

capital.heading: Fiji issued its first sovereign blue bond. Next, work that pays for every family.

register.name: Sovereign blue bond
register.detail: Issued 8 and 9 November 2023 · Three-year bonds at 1% and fifteen-year bonds at 4.2% · Bids above FJD 60M
register.text: Fiji’s first sovereign blue bond, issued with support from the UK Blue Planet Fund, UNDP and the Reserve Bank of Fiji. It funds nature-based coastal protection, aquaculture, sustainable towns and waste and wastewater management.

register.name: Fiji Growth and Resilience Second Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 25 June 2026 · Three World Bank commitments of $104.5M, $18M and $27.5M · Budget support
register.note: Budget support for growth and resilience
register.text: World Bank budget support for reforms to economic resilience, disaster preparedness and private-sector development, co-financed by the AIIB. Together the two provide $230 million of fast-disbursing support.

register.name: Critical Bridges Resilience Project
register.detail: Announced 24 January 2025 · World Bank $50M · ADB cofinancing $134.5M · Government of Fiji $15.06M
register.text: Makes four major bridges on the Queens Road from Suva to Lautoka (Medraukutu, Lami, Viseisei and Sabeto) resistant to natural hazards and climate change. They serve more than half a million people, about 62% of Fijians.

register.name: Sustainable and Resilient Growth Program, second phase
register.detail: Announced 16 September 2026 · $200M loan for policy reforms and $10M loan for disaster financing
register.text: ADB financing to help Fiji contain the effect of high energy prices and prepare for El Niño, with reforms that widen access to finance, strengthen disaster risk management, advance digital transformation and improve fiscal sustainability. It adds financing for a rapid government response to future emergencies.

register.name: Fiji Growth and Resilience Second Development Policy Financing, AIIB co-financing
register.detail: Approved 16 July 2026 · Energy, Food Security and Economic Resilience Facility · Sovereign-backed
register.text: The AIIB’s share of the $230 million of budget support with the World Bank, for economic and climate resilience and private-sector reforms. Targets for 2028 include wider disaster-risk-reduction plans, more small firms with access to regulated finance, more digital payments and better child nutrition referral.

register.name: Pacific Healthy Islands Transformation Project
register.detail: Announced 11 March 2026 · ADB concessional loan · Total $181.94M with the World Bank ($93.5M, lead), the OPEC Fund ($30M) and the Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response Trust Fund ($8.44M)
register.note: Primary care, digital health and a new referral hospital
register.text: Strengthens primary care and the response to noncommunicable diseases, brings digital clinical support and health information systems, and finances the first phase of a regional referral hospital and training facility at the Colonial War Memorial Hospital. It is the first Pacific project co-financed under the ADB–World Bank Full Mutual Reliance Framework: the health standard.

register.name: Enhancing Climate Resilience of Coastal Communities Sector Project
register.detail: Announced 17 December 2025 · Grant, $15M from the Asian Development Fund
register.text: Restores about 3,000 metres of coastline and riverbank with revegetation and mangroves and builds nature-based coastal protection for about 15 vulnerable communities. Protecting coastal communities serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Healthy Oceans and Water Security Improvement Project
register.detail: Announced 12 September 2025 · $125M concessional loan and $10M Asian Development Fund grant
register.text: Roughly doubles the capacity of the Kinoya wastewater treatment plant in Suva and continues a performance-based contract to cut water losses, saving about 10.5 million cubic metres a year, with a training hub in Lautoka. Run by the Water Authority of Fiji: the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Sustainable and Resilient Growth Program, first phase
register.detail: Signed 1 August 2024 · Policy-based concessional loan · Co-financed by Australia, New Zealand and the World Bank
register.note: Tax, public finance and disaster reforms
register.text: ADB budget support for reforms to the business and finance environment, revenue and public investment, gender-responsive budgeting and community disaster preparedness. Its second phase was approved in September 2026.

register.name: BRED Bank Fiji, risk-sharing facility for small businesses
register.detail: Announced 27 February 2026 · IFC Small Loan Guarantee Program · Up to FJD 27M of new loans
register.text: An unfunded IFC risk-sharing facility, supported by the IDA Private Sector Window, for new loans to small and medium enterprises, including on outer islands and in remote inland areas. Most work in agriculture, fisheries and small-scale tourism: the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 60 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Sugar cane fields in western Viti Levu, Fiji

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest in the highlands of Viti Levu, Fiji

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A turquoise lagoon and coral reef in Fiji

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A hydropower reservoir in the hills of Viti Levu, Fiji

items.name: Aspen Medical
items.text: Upgrades, runs and maintains Lautoka Hospital and Ba Hospital under a 23-year public-private partnership with the Government of Fiji: around 400 inpatient beds serving more than 365,000 people in the Western Division.

items.name: BRED Bank Fiji
items.text: Lending to small and medium enterprises across Fiji, including on outer islands and in remote inland communities, with an IFC risk-sharing facility for up to FJD 27 million of new loans.
